articles.dek: Wesley Fofana, as a former Leicester player, might have expected the celebrating Nottingham Forest fans to give him a hard time. But, at the end of a week in which he…
articles.description: Wesley Fofana, as a former Leicester player, might have expected the celebrating Nottingham Forest fans to give him a hard time. But, at the end of a week in which he invited opprobrium by making light of missing a penalty at Liverpool in an unsanctioned French interview, he endured the ultimate ignominy when Chelsea supporters followed a four-letter suggestion to tell the defender: “You’re not welcome here.” Fofana was humiliated by Liam Delap before fouling the former Chelsea striker for a penalty that Morgan Gibbs-White converted for the first of his two goals. The result, coming after Forest’s win against Manchester City in their last match at the City Ground, means they climb three points clear of the Premier League’s relegation zone. Continue reading...

articles.title: Why have things started to go wrong for Manchester City under Enzo Maresca?
articles.dek: A sensational start for the Italian was swiftly followed by a dismal run and long faces in the team This is the great known unknown in Manchester City’s run of one win –…
articles.description: A sensational start for the Italian was swiftly followed by a dismal run and long faces in the team This is the great known unknown in Manchester City’s run of one win – in addition to victory on penalties against Brighton in the Carabao Cup – in seven matches. After guilty verdicts were returned regarding the breaking of Premier League financial rules, Enzo Maresca’s team went to Anfield and handed Liverpool a 3-0 schooling . Yet this proved the falsest of dawns, with Andoni Iraola’s nascent side perhaps caught in a bad moment. City have since managed one league victory ( 3-2 over Ipswich , six days later) and two more wins in regulation time (in the Champions League) in 10 matches. The sequence includes one point from the past four league fixtures. Maresca argues that his, too, is an embryonic project so there will be uneven form. “I am not a magician,” he said on Friday. But it is also fair to ponder whether, after the adrenaline surge of an us-against-the-world mentality carried City to the Liverpool and Ipswich wins, the grim reality of what the guilty verdict may mean for careers is affecting players. City have appealed against the ruling, saying they are “innocent of the accusations”. Continue reading...

“I am not a magician,” he said on Friday. But it is also fair to ponder whether, after the adrenaline surge of an us-against-the-world mentality carried City to the Liverpool and Ipswich wins, the grim reality of what the guilty verdict may mean for careers is affecting players. articles.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! A few weeks ago, Alessio Dionisi was forced to deny the “fake news” he had joined Sean Dyche, Gianfranco Zola, Beppe Sannino, Óscar García, Billy McKinlay, Slavisa Jokanovic, Quique Sánchez Flores (twice), Walter Mazzarri, Marco Silva, Javi Gracia (twice), Nigel Pearson, Vladimir Ivic, Xisco Muñoz, Claudio Ranieri, Roy Hodgson, Rob Edwards, Slaven Bilic, Chris Wilder, Valérien Ismael, Tom Cleverley, Paulo Pezzolano and Edward Still in being sacked by the Pozzo family since 2012. There was no denial on Sunday, when the axe inevitably fell on the head coach following a 4-0 shellacking at Sheffield United and the Italian left after only 18 games in charge. While his reign is unlikely to live long in the memory of anyone at Vicarage Road, Dionisi can at least boast on his LinkedIn page that in terms of longevity under the Pozzos, he took charge of 18 more matches than Dyche, 17 more than García and 16 more than McKinlay. Indeed, he even outlasted Rob Edwards, who was assured he would be backed “come hell or high water” upon his 2022 appointment, only to be fired from the ejector seat 11 games later. Club activate option and plan further talks with captain ‘I am not nice,’ says Pochettino as he targets improvement Manchester United have triggered a clause to extend the captain Bruno Fernandes’ contract until the summer of 2028 on a day when Mauricio Pochettino warned his players they should not expect him to be “nice” in his attempts to turn around the club’s fortunes. Fernandes’ deal was due to expire in June and by exercising the option United have avoided the risk from January that he could negotiate a pre-contract agreement with a club abroad to join on a free next summer. Fernandes said this month that talks over a longer extension were on hold “because of the context of the team and the club”.
He has turned down two United contract offers. Continue reading...
